chapter_title: Chương 64: Trần Quý Lương Nổi Tiếng Trên Mạng

segments.title: Chương 64: Trần Quý Lương Nổi Tiếng Trên Mạng
segments.content:
"Young man, you need more practice with your brush calligraphy."

Dong Hongkang carefully put the poem away and shook hands with Chen Guiliang. "Today has been very meaningful. I'll have someone mount this poem. You don't hold it against me, do you?"

Chen Guiliang smiled faintly. "Thank you, Editor Dong, for giving me this chance to become famous."

"Hahaha," Dong Hongkang laughed heartily, slapping Chen Guiliang on the shoulder. "Wait for the paper in two days. I'm off!"

Hu Weishi tried to detain him. "Editor Dong, there's still a banquet."

"I'll skip the meal. Goodbye!" Dong Hongkang left as soon as he said it.

Many of the editors and reporters at the *Bihui* were like this, straightforward and brisk in both their words and actions.

*The Scar*, the work that pioneered Scar literature, was first published in *Bihui*.

Bian Qin, the author of *A Subverted Civilization* and *Who is Directing the World*, had also been a long-time columnist for *Bihui* since 2004. (These two books are critiques of Western cultural hegemony.)

In addition, the first article Ba Jin published after *The Torrent of Humanity* was also in *Bihui*. Before he died, Ba Jin's very last article was published in *Bihui* as well.

This showed that *Bihui* couldn't be simply defined as left-leaning or right-leaning.

This supplement was extremely influential, and many leaders were long-term subscribers!

Dong Hongkang drove back to the newspaper office. There was still half an hour left before the end of the workday.

"What's got you so happy? You're beaming," asked Zhou Yi, a senior editor at the next desk.

Zhou Yi's pen name was Fang Fei, and she was due for a promotion to deputy chief editor in two years.

Dong Hongkang smiled. "You have a young fellow townsman who writes quite well."

"What young fellow townsman?" Zhou Yi asked.

Dong Hongkang said, "From Longdu City."

Zhou Yi chuckled. "That's quite close indeed, right next to my hometown. Have there been any traditional writers from there in recent years? There was only Wei Minglun, and he just worked in Longdu and was transferred away long ago."

Longdu City was indeed not very impressive at the moment. For now, it only had Guo Xiaosi.

Abstract figures like Huang Xudong were probably still in university.

There was another female writer who was about to become famous this year, Rao Xueman, the author of *The Left Ear*.

Dong Hongkang took out the *A Voyage on the Sea* printed by the competition organizers. "A first-prize essay from the New Concept Competition."

Zhou Yi's eyes lit up as she read it, but then she became skeptical. "The quality of this prose poem is too high. Is it really genuine?"

"That's why I tested him on the spot," Dong Hongkang said, taking out the second poem, quite pleased with himself. "The title of this poem is 'A Reply to Editor Dong of <Bihui>.' I gave him four words—wild goose, small boat, river water, and time—and asked him to write a classical poem."

After reading it, Zhou Yi lightly slapped the desk. "A fine poem, excellent literary talent. We should ask him for more submissions in the future, poems or prose, either will do."

"I plan to give him a full page! I'll publish both of his poems in full and write a commentary," Dong Hongkang said.

Zhou Yi asked, "What day will it be in the paper?"

Dong Hongkang said, "The day after tomorrow."

"We might not have enough space the day after tomorrow. How about giving him two-thirds of a page?" Zhou Yi suggested.

Dong Hongkang said, "That works too."

The two chatted until it was time to leave work, then each went home for dinner.

After a quick meal, Dong Hongkang hurried to his study to write a commentary on Chen Guiliang's two poems.

He had only written two or three hundred words when the deputy chief editor, Liu Xuyuan, called. "Xiao Dong, you've made an appearance on the Rì Yuè Guāng Huá BBS."

"What Rì Yuè Guāng Huá?" Dong Hongkang didn't understand.

Liu Xuyuan said, "Fudan's campus forum. I'm a Fudan alumnus too, you know, so I browse the forum when I have free time. I saw you as soon as I logged in today. Something about composing a poem in seven steps. You've become the villain of the story."

"Hahaha, the news travels that fast?" Dong Hongkang found it hilarious.

"Log in and see for yourself. Quite a few students are cursing you out," Liu Xuyuan said.

The news had spread from the *Mengya* forum.

The main users of this forum were middle school students, but there were also many university students and young adults.

The atmosphere on the forum was relatively harmonious.

The only few times a group flame war broke out, it was centered around Guo Xiaosi.

Because the New Concept Writing Competition was currently underway, the *Mengya* forum had been especially active these past few days.

Some contestants took the initiative to share what they had seen and heard. Meanwhile, the vast number of middle school students with literary dreams eagerly asked all sorts of questions under the sharing threads.

This very noon, a post had gone viral: *Ten Prestigious Universities Fought Over Someone Last Night, We Were All Stunned.*

"I won a first prize this time, and I had the chance to inquire about admissions information from the prestigious universities last night. The situation this year is terrible. Not only did Tsinghua have no slots, but Nanjing University and Sun Yat-sen University didn't have any either..."

"But there was this one guy, no idea what he wrote, who was being fought over like crazy by all the schools on the spot."

"Tsinghua, which had no slots, promised to hold a meeting to discuss a special admission for him. Nanjing University and Sun Yat-sen University, also without slots, said they could squeeze one out for him. Peking University promised to admit him if he passed the Tier 1 cutoff score, Fudan promised admission if he passed the undergraduate cutoff score, and Beijing Normal, East China Normal, and Xiamen University offered him direct admission without exams..."

"You have no idea how ridiculous it was. That Director Yan from Beijing Normal University even mentioned guaranteed admission to their master's and doctoral programs. The guy could pick any major he wanted if he went there..."

"By the way, his name is Chen Guiliang, and he's an alumnus of Guo Xiaosi's school."

This afternoon, while the symposium was still in session, this post on the *Mengya* forum had already accumulated several hundred replies.

"OP is bullshitting, confirmed."

"If I'm bullshitting, may my whole family die!"

"OP is really committed to his bullshit, even put his family on the line."

"I can vouch for it. Although I only got an honorable mention and didn't have the chance to see it in person, I heard the news last night and specifically went to Chen Guiliang's room to join the excitement. There were so many people there I couldn't even squeeze through the door."

"It's true. I got a second prize, and my home is in Taicang. I wasn't qualified to receive my award on stage today; the certificate was given out privately in the morning. I took a bus home right after getting it, and I just arrived. Anyway, I can't imagine what he wrote. I heard it was a classical poem."

"Why do I feel like you guys are all making this up together?"

"I live in Yangpu, Shanghai. Second prize, rematched number A009. The people above aren't lying. I've been staying at home these few days. I went to pick up my certificate this morning and heard about what happened last night. It sounds fake, but it's really true."

"I'm from Xuhui, honorable mention, rematched number A015. I also heard about this this morning."

"..."

More and more contestants replied, each describing it vividly.

Gradually, no one doubted it anymore. Instead, they asked for details and discussed the matter enthusiastically.

"What on earth did he write? Just for one classical poem? I could do that too."

"There's definitely something shady going on. Maybe the topic was leaked in advance and he had someone ghostwrite it for him."

"Or maybe his family has connections."

"We asked yesterday. He chose the second prompt. For those newbies who don't know the prompts, you can check another thread. He used a classical poem to write an allegory. The little bird symbolized the benevolent and determined people throughout history, the tree branch symbolized the resilient spirit of Chinese civilization, and the ocean waves symbolized the thousands of years of calamities China has faced."

"That's it?"

"I don't get it."

"It must be because his essay was well-written. Even if one admissions officer had a screw loose, could all of them be fools?"

"Let's just wait and see. It will definitely be included in the selected works anthology."

"I'm going to enter next year too, and fight for a recommendation to Tsinghua or Peking!"

"To the person above, it's not dark yet. You might have a better chance if you dream about it tonight."

"..."

In the evening, Li Haiyang rushed into an internet cafe and posted: *Seven-Step Poem Composed on the Spot at the New Concept Competition. Are You Impressed or What!*

"I'm first prize winner A071, just left the hotel, posting from a nearby internet cafe. There was more big news at the symposium this afternoon. Dong Hongkang, editor of the *Wenhui Bao*'s *Bihui* supplement, questioned the high quality of Chen Guiliang's rematched essay and challenged him on the spot to compose a poem."

"I won't post his two poems for now, I'll just give you Editor Dong's prompt. Try writing it yourselves. Using the four images of wild goose, small boat, river water, and time, write a classical poem."

The previous thread was already very popular, and Li Haiyang's post quickly got replies.

"Challenged him on the spot? That's so disrespectful."

"Damn. If it were me, I would have been stunned speechless."

"Is this Dong guy nuts?"

"Judging by the title, Chen Guiliang composed it in seven steps?"

"Let me try. *A wild goose cleaves the sky on its southward flight, a guest boat tows the setting sun's red light. I wish to send a letter on the flowing stream, but the west wind first tucks it in the flowering reeds.*"

"Nice poem from the person above."

"Me too, me too. *Misty waves carry the journey home, the wild goose flies with the evening glow. At the ferry, spring waters are green, the oar sways with a youth's heart, keen.*"

"OMG, you guys are all so talented. I'm still in my third year of middle school, how do you learn to write classical poetry?"

"OP is an ass, post Chen Guiliang's poem if you know what's good for you. I want to see what he's made of, to be wanted by ten prestigious universities."

"..."

Seeing that the thread had over twenty replies, Li Haiyang finally posted Chen Guiliang's poem, deliberately omitting the details about him stalling for time:

"Let me recreate the scene for you. When Editor Dong gave the prompt, many people were sweating for Chen Guiliang. Then we heard Chen Guiliang shout: 'Sister Weishi, brush, ink, paper, and inkstone!'"

"The staff brought the writing materials, Chen Guiliang took seven steps, picked up the brush, and wrote: *The boat sails on misty waters vast, the wild goose passes evening clouds' edge. This life is but a transient stay, why ask about the passing years?*"

After hitting enter and sending the post, Li Haiyang refreshed the page.

Although he saw new replies, they were unrelated to the poem. He refreshed another four or five times.

"Awesome!"

"So amazing."

"This one is just average, not much different from what the netizens above wrote."

"Hey, person above, why don't you try writing one?"

"So well written, definitely has real skill."

"Vast is an adjective, edge is a noun. The parallelism isn't perfect, it's flawed."

"Bro, you're just nitpicking."

"I'm from the Chinese department at Wuhan University, and I have a rudimentary understanding of classical poetry. Words of different parts of speech can still form a parallel couplet. For example, Du Fu's 'Stars hang over the vast, flat wilds; the moon bobs on the great, flowing river.' Vast is an adjective, and flowing is a verb, but they still form a parallel couplet, complementing each other with spatial dynamics. In Chen Guiliang's poem, vast and edge, although different parts of speech, can form a spatial couplet. This is known as a 'broad couplet'."

"Wow, you're amazing, GG, you must be a literary talent from Wuhan University!"

"Senior, I want to apply to Wuhan University too."

"Great talent, could you explain this poem?"

"Hold on, I need to check some reference books."

The replies continued, but the literary talent from Wuhan University went silent, probably off to look up information.

A few minutes later, the Wuhan University talent posted again: "Strictly speaking, the last two lines violate the tonal rules, the character 'shēn' creates a 'solitary level tone.' You would just need to change 'běn nì lǚ' to 'rú nì lǚ,' and it would be perfectly saved in conjunction with the fourth line. But I don't think it needs changing, the meaning is conveyed, and changing it would lose that transcendent, composed flavor. The author probably did it on purpose, otherwise, he wouldn't have altered the original phrase when alluding to it."

"I don't get it."

"What's a solitary level tone?"

"Are the tones for 'rú' and 'běn' different?"

"I think I'll stick to writing modern poetry."

"You and Chen Guiliang are both so amazing."

"A bunch of old fogeys. Who even writes classical poetry nowadays?"

"..."

The literary talent from Wuhan University posted again: "OP, could you post Chen Guiliang's rematched essay?"

"Hold on." Li Haiyang copied and pasted it into a new Word document.

The Wuhan University talent refreshed the page four times before finally seeing Chen Guiliang's *A Voyage on the Sea*.

He stared at the computer screen for a long time, repeatedly typing and deleting several times, before finally replying with just two words: "Holy shit!"

Immediately after, he quickly copied and pasted the poem, posting it to Wuhan University's Luòjiā Shānshuǐ BBS.
